scenarios.title: First-Party Browser Wallet
scenarios.summary: A fresh internal Rust wallet control claims and stores the configured credential, presents it for login, and proves closed-session rejection.

revision_history.superseded_reason: Replace the historical placeholder with a dedicated current-run control contract: governed claim, receipt and storage, authenticated presentation, and closed-session rejection. Credential format is observed rather than inferred.

poster.alt: Draft release card for the first-party Rust wallet control; fresh capture is required

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: An eligible synthetic member claims a credential through the product. This recording uses the internal first-party Rust wallet control.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The wallet receives the canonical offer and shows the expected stored credential. The actual receipt identifies its credential format.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: After signing out, the member starts credential login. The wallet presents the credential, and ElevenID creates a new authenticated session without another password.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: The run's wallet session is then closed. A later credential-list request returns HTTP 410, confirming closed-session rejection for this internal control.

assertions.label: The synthetic holder claims through the product and signs out before credential login.
The Rust control receives and displays the expected credential with its actual format.
A real presentation and HTTP 200 authentication check establish a new session.
After exact owned session closure, the run-bound credential-list API rejects access with HTTP 410.

limitations: This is the internal FIRST_PARTY_CONTROL and reuses the governed membership product path. It does not qualify a public wallet product.
The negative boundary is closed-session rejection through the Rust API; TTL expiry and public-device isolation are not claimed.
The approved synthetic application and deployed issuer, trust and credential-login resources are preprovisioned dependencies. Wallet session closure is not server credential revocation.
The fixed entrypoint and full capture revision must be bound to the deployed source, with two fresh recordings and this scenario's own report. Historical or D03/D05 media are not inherited.
Current live capture, measured voice/captions/crops/pointers, privacy review and publication remain unqualified.

scenarios.title: Independent Wallet Interoperability
scenarios.summary: Two fresh pinned native Spruce runs exercise governed credential receipt, unchanged signed DCQL presentation, authenticated login, and holder cancellation without a browser session.

revision_history.superseded_reason: Replace the retained placeholder with a dedicated current native Spruce issuance, signed-request presentation, authentication and holder-cancel contract. Each lane requires its own fresh evidence.

poster.alt: Draft release card for pinned native wallet interoperability; fresh two-lane capture is required

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Synthetic test data and AI-generated narration. A member uses a pinned Spruce wallet to receive a credential and access ElevenID.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Stage one: issue. Claim through the product, select the registered Spruce wallet, and add the fresh credential to the native wallet.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Stage two: present. Sign out and start credential login. The product supplies its unchanged signed request with a DCQL query.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Review the request and select Approve. The operator then explicitly returns to Chrome, as shown in the recording.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Stage three: authenticate. The same browser confirms ElevenID created a new authenticated session after native presentation.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Stage four: cancel. A separate clean wallet run receives a fresh credential and starts another credential-login request.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: Select Cancel and explicitly return to the same Chrome session. Its authentication check must show that no session was created.

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: These two paths cover one pinned wallet. Other vendors, credential formats and physical-device security need separate evidence.

chapters.title: Issue into a clean native wallet
Cancel in a separate fresh lane

assertions.label: A clean pinned Spruce wallet receives a fresh credential through the governed product claim.
The native wallet handles the product's unchanged signed DCQL request and the holder approves presentation.
The same previously signed-out Chrome session observes successful authentication after native presentation.
A separate clean native run receives its own credential, cancels consent, and confirms that Chrome remains unauthenticated.

limitations: This current contract covers one pinned Spruce implementation with separate fresh happy and holder-cancel lanes. It does not qualify other vendors, exact credential formats or disclosed-claim inventories.

The supported transport is the product's existing native-intent fallback in a frozen Chrome profile where Digital Credentials transport is unsupported. A chooser profile remains BLOCKED; feature detection and signed requests are not overridden.
The native wallet returns to its own home screen. Recorder-driven return to Chrome is explicit and recorded; automatic browser callback behavior is not claimed.

Each lane needs a distinct fresh synthetic account, no existing same-template application, an empty isolated wallet, active governed issuance/login resources and matching deployed source. Existing applications are not repurposed.
The adapter binds the original request form and hashes; it does not independently reverify the request signature. Native Rust protocol verification remains the wallet and product's responsibility.
The two native recordings, reports and final session observations must belong to this scenario's current run. No historical, first-party, D03 or D05 report is inherited.
Server credential retirement, physical-device security, measured voice/captions/crops/pointers, privacy review and publication are outside the local source checks and remain pending.
